title: MovieDB Watchlist (repo debugging)
src: Amazon SDE Intern OA 2026 · section 2, repository debugging (MERN)
body:
MovieDB is an app where users explore movies, rate them and write reviews. The watchlist feature lets a user save movies to watch later. It is broken on the backend.

Issue: users can add movies to their watchlist, but the movies never appear on the Watchlist page. Removing a movie, either from the Watchlist page or by toggling Add to Watchlist on the movie page, doesn't work either. Fix the backend of the watchlist feature.

Additional requirement: to stop spam, each user may add or remove movies at most 10 times in any 2-minute window, with adds and removes counted together.

The acceptance criteria are the predefined tests. Use the failing ones to guide your debugging. The repo may also contain issues unrelated to this task; leave those alone.

Expected API (README.md)

Every route needs Authorization: Bearer <token>. authMiddleware sets req.userId or answers 401.

RouteSuccessErrors
GET /api/watchlist/200, an array of the user's movie documents in the order they were added500 Server error
GET /api/watchlist/check/:movieId200 {"isInWatchlist": true|false}400 Invalid movie ID format
POST /api/watchlist/add
body {"movieId"}		201 Movie added to watchlist successfully400 Movie ID is required · 400 Invalid movie ID format · 404 Movie not found · 400 Movie already in watchlist · 429 rate limit
POST /api/watchlist/remove
body {"movieId"}		200 Movie removed from watchlist successfully400 Movie ID is required · 400 Invalid movie ID format · 404 Movie not found in watchlist · 429 rate limit

The 429 body is {"message": "Too many watchlist operations. You can add or remove movies up to 10 times within 2 minutes."}. The limiter runs before the controller, so every add or remove request it lets through counts, even one that then fails validation. A request rejected with 429 does not count. A request made at time t stops counting once now − t ≥ 2 minutes.

When a movie is added or removed, the watchlist entry must really be created in or deleted from the database.

How the tests work

The editor holds three files from the repo: controllers/watchlistController.js, middleware/rateLimiter.js and routes/watchlistRoutes.js. On every run a fresh database is seeded and a test client sends requests to the app. Each test is a script, one request per line:

<seconds since start> <sam | alex | -> <GET|POST> <url> [JSON body]

- sends no token. For each request the client prints the status code and the JSON body. For the watchlist list it prints only the movie titles, so 200 ["Interstellar"] means one movie document whose title is Interstellar. Lines starting with [log] are server logs, such as console.error output. They are shown to help you and are ignored when grading. Tick Custom input to send your own request script.

The rest of the repo is read-only. Its files are below.

// ---- file: framework (read-only) ----------------------------------------
// Small stand-ins for express and mongoose so the repo runs in the browser.
// import/export lines are removed; every file shares one scope.
const __out = [];
const __log = (...a) => __out.push("[log] " + a.map(x => x instanceof Error ? (x.name + ": " + x.message) : typeof x === "string" ? x : JSON.stringify(x)).join(" "));
console = Object.assign({}, console, {log: __log, info: __log, warn: __log, error: __log});

const mongoose = { Types: { ObjectId: { isValid: id => typeof id === "string" && /^[0-9a-f]{24}$/i.test(id) } } };

const express = {
  Router() {
    const r = { stack: [] };
    r.use = fn => { r.stack.push({ all: true, h: [fn] }); return r; };
    for (const m of ["get", "post", "put", "delete"]) r[m] = (path, ...h) => { r.stack.push({ method: m.toUpperCase(), path, h }); return r; };
    return r;
  }
};

// ---- file: models/Movie.js (read-only) ----------------------------------
const MOVIES = [
  { _id: "65f0a1b2c3d4e5f600000001", title: "The Shawshank Redemption", year: 1994, rating: 9.3, genre: ["Drama", "Crime"] },
  { _id: "65f0a1b2c3d4e5f600000002", title: "Interstellar", year: 2014, rating: 8.7, genre: ["Sci-Fi", "Drama"] },
  { _id: "65f0a1b2c3d4e5f600000003", title: "The Dark Knight", year: 2008, rating: 9.0, genre: ["Action", "Crime"] },
  { _id: "65f0a1b2c3d4e5f600000004", title: "Spirited Away", year: 2001, rating: 8.6, genre: ["Animation", "Fantasy"] },
  { _id: "65f0a1b2c3d4e5f600000005", title: "Parasite", year: 2019, rating: 8.5, genre: ["Thriller", "Drama"] },
  { _id: "65f0a1b2c3d4e5f600000006", title: "Inception", year: 2010, rating: 8.8, genre: ["Sci-Fi", "Action"] }
];
const Movie = {
  async findById(id) { const m = MOVIES.find(x => x._id === String(id)); return m ? { ...m } : null; },
  async find() { return MOVIES.map(m => ({ ...m })); }
};

// ---- file: models/Watchlist.js (read-only) ------------------------------
// Schema: { user: ObjectId, movie: ObjectId -> Movie }, unique index on (user, movie).
// Supported: create, find(filter) [+ .populate("movie")], findOne(filter), findOneAndDelete(filter), deleteOne(filter)
const __rows = []; let __seq = 0;
const __match = (row, f) => Object.keys(f || {}).every(k => String(row[k]) === String(f[k]));
const __copy = r => ({ ...r });
const Watchlist = {
  async create(doc) {
    if (__rows.some(r => r.user === String(doc.user) && r.movie === String(doc.movie))) {
      const e = new Error("E11000 duplicate key error collection: watchlists index: user_1_movie_1"); e.code = 11000; throw e;
    }
    const row = { _id: "77aa00000000000000" + String(++__seq).padStart(6, "0"), user: String(doc.user), movie: String(doc.movie), createdAt: new Date(Date.now()).toISOString() };
    __rows.push(row); return __copy(row);
  },
  find(filter) {
    let pop = false;
    const q = {
      populate(field) { if (field === "movie") pop = true; return q; },
      then(ok, bad) {
        return (async () => {
          const rows = __rows.filter(r => __match(r, filter)).map(__copy);
          if (pop) for (const r of rows) r.movie = await Movie.findById(r.movie);
          return rows;
        })().then(ok, bad);
      }
    };
    return q;
  },
  async findOne(filter) { const r = __rows.find(x => __match(x, filter)); return r ? __copy(r) : null; },
  async findOneAndDelete(filter) { const i = __rows.findIndex(x => __match(x, filter)); return i < 0 ? null : __copy(__rows.splice(i, 1)[0]); },
  async deleteOne(filter) { const i = __rows.findIndex(x => __match(x, filter)); if (i >= 0) __rows.splice(i, 1); return { deletedCount: i < 0 ? 0 : 1 }; }
};

// ---- file: middleware/auth.js (read-only) -------------------------------
const USERS = { "token-sam": "64aa0000000000000000a001", "token-alex": "64aa0000000000000000a002" };
const authMiddleware = (req, res, next) => {
  const h = req.headers.authorization || "";
  const userId = USERS[h.replace(/^Bearer /, "")];
  if (!userId) return res.status(401).json({ message: "No token, authorization denied" });
  req.userId = userId;
  next();
};

Read-only file: app.js and the test client
// ---- file: app.js + test client (read-only) -----------------------------
return (async () => {
  const realNow = Date.now;
  let clock = 1767225600000;            // 2026-01-01T00:00:00Z
  Date.now = () => clock;
  const router = (typeof watchlistRouter !== "undefined") ? watchlistRouter : null;
  if (!router) { __out.push("watchlistRouter is not defined"); return; }
  const matchPath = (pat, path) => {
    const a = pat.replace(/\/+$/, "").split("/"), b = path.replace(/\/+$/, "").split("/");
    if (a.length !== b.length) return null;
    const params = {};
    for (let i = 0; i < a.length; i++) {
      if (a[i].startsWith(":")) params[a[i].slice(1)] = decodeURIComponent(b[i]);
      else if (a[i] !== b[i]) return null;
    }
    return params;
  };
  const show = body => {
    if (Array.isArray(body)) return JSON.stringify(body.map(x => x && typeof x === "object" && typeof x.title === "string" ? x.title : x));
    return JSON.stringify(body === undefined ? null : body);
  };
  async function request(method, url, user, body) {
    const sub = url.replace(/^\/api\/watchlist/, "") || "/";
    const req = { method, path: sub, originalUrl: url, params: {}, body: body || {}, headers: user === "-" ? {} : { authorization: "Bearer token-" + user } };
    let sent = null;
    const res = {
      statusCode: 200,
      status(c) { this.statusCode = c; return this; },
      json(b) { if (sent) { __log("Error [ERR_HTTP_HEADERS_SENT]: Cannot set headers after they are sent to the client"); return this; } sent = { code: this.statusCode, body: b }; return this; },
      send(b) { return this.json(b); }
    };
    const layers = router.stack.filter(l => l.all || (l.method === method && matchPath(l.path, sub)));
    const chain = [];
    for (const l of layers) { if (!l.all) req.params = matchPath(l.path, sub); for (const h of l.h) chain.push(h); }
    const routed = layers.some(l => !l.all);
    const run = async i => {
      if (sent) return;
      if (i >= chain.length) { if (!routed) res.status(404).json({ message: "Cannot " + method + " " + url }); return; }
      let p;
      try { p = chain[i](req, res, () => run(i + 1)); if (p && typeof p.then === "function") await p; }
      catch (e) { __log(e); if (!sent) res.status(500).json({ message: "Internal Server Error" }); }
    };
    await run(0);
    for (let k = 0; k < 5 && !sent; k++) await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 0));
    return sent || { code: 504, body: { message: "No response: the request never finished (it would time out)" } };
  }
  try {
  const lines = require("fs").readFileSync().split("\n").map(l => l.trim()).filter(l => l && !l.startsWith("#"));
  for (const line of lines) {
    const m = line.match(/^(\d+)\s+(\S+)\s+(GET|POST)\s+(\S+)\s*(.*)$/);
    if (!m) { __out.push("bad test line: " + line); continue; }
    clock = 1767225600000 + Number(m[1]) * 1000;
    let body = {};
    if (m[5]) body = JSON.parse(m[5]);
    const r = await request(m[3], m[4], m[2], body);
    __out.push(r.code + " " + show(r.body));
  }
  } finally { Date.now = realNow; }
  process.stdout.write(__out.join("\n") + "\n");
})();
inp: A request script (see How the tests work). The repo's test client reads it, so you don't parse input yourself.
out: One line per request: <status> <JSON body>, printed by the test client.
cons: Edit only the three files in the editor; the framework, models, auth and test client are fixed
Language: JavaScript (the real repo is Node + Express + MongoDB)
The tests run against an in-memory database seeded fresh on every run

samples.ex: Adding Interstellar returns 201, and the watchlist then lists it. The buggy repo returns 500 for the list.

samples.in:
# Watchlist status is a boolean
0 sam GET /api/watchlist/check/65f0a1b2c3d4e5f600000002
1 sam POST /api/watchlist/add {"movieId":"65f0a1b2c3d4e5f600000002"}
2 sam GET /api/watchlist/check/65f0a1b2c3d4e5f600000002
3 sam GET /api/watchlist/check/abc
samples.ex: check must return true or false, not the array that find() gives back.

fixnotes:
• getWatchlist called Watchlist.findByUser, which doesn't exist, so the list always failed with 500. Use Watchlist.find({ user: userId }).populate('movie') so the response contains movie documents, not ids.
  • addToWatchlist answered 201 but never called Watchlist.create. A duplicate must answer 400 Movie already in watchlist. Answering 404 here was a common mistake; the unique index's error code 11000 is a second safety net.
  • removeFromWatchlist never deleted anything and never answered 404. Use findOneAndDelete and check the result.
  • checkWatchlistStatus returned the array from find. It must return a boolean: !!(await Watchlist.findOne(...)).
  • watchlistRateLimiter: windowMs was never defined (ReferenceError, so 500). The filter kept the expired timestamps (>= instead of <). if (requests) is always true because an empty array is truthy. validRequests was never declared. It should be: keep timestamps with now − t < 2 min, reject when 10 or more remain, otherwise push now.
  • The routes never used the limiter. Wiring watchlistRateLimiter without calling it passes the factory as middleware, so the request hangs (the real test runner showed a 20 s timeout). Use watchlistRateLimiter(). The generic rateLimiter keys by path, so it would count adds and removes separately; it isn't the right tool here.
